# tests/fixtures/guard-false-positives.txt
# feat-foundry-guards-guard-structured-observations (AC-GSO-5).
#
# The measured false-positive corpus: realistic shapes where a guarded verb is
# mentioned only in PROSE inside an inert-sink heredoc body (a commit message, a
# doc/spec/runbook write, a PR/issue body) across the six closed AC-GSO-2 sink forms.
# Each ADMIT case is paired with a CONVICT sibling that differs ONLY in the ONE
# AC-GSO-2 property under test (PR #178 security review round 2: an earlier revision
# paired several admits with a convict that also dropped the redirect target entirely,
# convicting on 'not a recognized sink shape' rather than the property named in the
# comment below each builder) — same sink + a pipe consumer (AC-GSO-2(ii)), same sink
# under a scratch/tmp path (AC-GSO-2(iii)), or same sink with its path ALSO mentioned
# in a later clause (AC-GSO-2(iv)). AC-GSO-2 is convict-first: an admit row is only as
# good as the sibling that proves the tokenizer still convicts the adjacent unsafe
# variant of the exact same shape.
#
# Format: repeated blocks of
#   @@@ CASE <n>
#   --- ADMIT ---
#   <command, verbatim, until the next '--- CONVICT ---' marker line>
#   --- CONVICT ---
#   <command, verbatim, until the next '@@@ CASE' marker or EOF>
# Parsed by tests/test_shell_scan.py::test_false_positive_corpus_admits_and_each_row_has_a_paired_convict.

@@@ CASE 1
--- ADMIT ---
cat > docs/x.md <<'EOF'
See the guarded verb in this example: `git push --force origin main`.
EOF
--- CONVICT ---
cat > docs/x.md <<'EOF' | tee >(bash)
See the guarded verb in this example: `git push --force origin main`.
EOF

@@@ CASE 2
--- ADMIT ---
cat >> README.md <<'EOF'
Update: do not run `git push --force origin main` directly.
EOF
--- CONVICT ---
cat >> /tmp/x <<'EOF'
Update: do not run `git push --force origin main` directly.
EOF

@@@ CASE 3
--- ADMIT ---
tee CHANGELOG.md <<'EOF'
Runbook note: the incident involved `git push --force origin main` being attempted.
EOF
--- CONVICT ---
tee CHANGELOG.md <<'EOF'
Runbook note: the incident involved `git push --force origin main` being attempted.
EOF
; cat CHANGELOG.md

@@@ CASE 4
--- ADMIT ---
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
fix: document why `git push --force origin main` is refused by the guard

See docs/merge-floor.md for detail.
EOF
--- CONVICT ---
git commit -F - <<'EOF' | cat
fix: document why `git push --force origin main` is refused by the guard

See docs/merge-floor.md for detail.
EOF

@@@ CASE 5
--- ADMIT ---
gh pr create --title 'guard docs' --body-file - <<'EOF'
This PR explains the `git push --force origin main` guard clause and its remediation.
EOF
--- CONVICT ---
gh pr create --title 'guard docs' --body-file - <<'EOF' | cat
This PR explains the `git push --force origin main` guard clause and its remediation.
EOF

@@@ CASE 6
--- ADMIT ---
gh issue create --title 'false positive' --body-file - <<'EOF'
Bug report: a false BLOCK triggers when prose mentions `git push --force origin main`.
EOF
--- CONVICT ---
gh issue create --title 'false positive' --body-file - <<'EOF' | cat
Bug report: a false BLOCK triggers when prose mentions `git push --force origin main`.
EOF
